summary: This informational RFC assigns a Generic Associated Channel type for carrying ITU-T MPLS-TP OAM messages in the MPLS Generic Associated Channel.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6671 assigns a channel type for carrying a specific set of ITU-T maintenance messages over MPLS. The assignment is limited to those messages and does not mean the IETF endorses that OAM solution.

subtitle: IANA assigns a Generic Associated Channel type to ITU-T MPLS-TP OAM messages.

tldr.problem: ITU-T Recommendation G.8113.1 messages need a Generic Associated Channel type to be carried in MPLS in an interoperable way.
tldr.mechanism: IANA assigns type 0x8902 for G.8113.1 OAM messages. The type is restricted to messages addressing the OAM functional requirements in RFC 5860.
tldr.outcome: The assignment does not endorse the alternate OAM solution; the IESG note recommends implementing the IETF OAM RFCs listed in RFC 6669.

today: RFC 6671 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Channel Type Was Assigned
sections.content: The ITU-T Recommendation G.8113.1 defines Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) messages for MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP). To carry those messages in the MPLS Generic Associated Channel, an assigned channel type is needed. IANA assigned 0x8902 for this purpose so the messages would not use an experimental type.
sections.plainLanguage: G.8113.1 defines maintenance messages for MPLS-TP. IANA assigned a channel type so those messages can be identified when carried in the Generic Associated Channel.

sections.title: Limits on the Assigned Type
sections.content: The assigned type MUST be used only for OAM messages defined in G.8113.1 and carried in the Generic Associated Channel. Those messages and procedures are limited to the OAM functional requirements in RFC 5860. Other message types MUST NOT be carried using this type. It may be used on transport constructs that use the Generic Associated Channel.
sections.plainLanguage: The assigned type is only for the specified OAM messages. Other message types must not use it.

sections.title: Registry Entry and IESG Note
sections.content: IANA added value 0x8902 to the Pseudowire Associated Channel Types subregistry. The entry is named G.8113.1 OAM and says no TLV follows. The IESG note states that assigning the type does not constitute IETF endorsement of the alternate OAM described in G.8113.1, and recommends implementation of the IETF OAM tools referenced in RFC 6669.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry identifies 0x8902 as G.8113.1 OAM. The IESG note says the assignment is not an endorsement and recommends the IETF OAM tools.
